description: A college dean of students must finalize a student's re-entry plan after a residence-hall vandalism case, including the sanction, restitution, housing assignment, conduct-meeting format, counseling support, and required safeguards, with input from conduct, residence-life, and counseling staff.

shared_context.S1: A student was found responsible for damaging common-area property in a residence hall and is scheduled to return to campus next week.
shared_context.S2: Dr. Morgan has final authority to approve the student's re-entry plan.
shared_context.S3: The draft case packet recommends a 10-day suspension, $500 restitution, return to the student's current room, in-person conduct check-ins, and a general counseling referral.
shared_context.S4: At weekly re-entry case conferences, Dr. Morgan follows the normal procedure of asking the conduct officer, residence-life coordinator, and counseling director for any case information that should be included before the plan is signed.

PF1.text: Ms. Ellis reviewed the student's complete conduct history and confirmed this is the student's first substantiated conduct violation; under the applicable policy, the student qualifies for a restorative agreement with exactly $250 in restitution instead of suspension. She completed the review after the draft packet was circulated, so the updated determination is not yet in the packet.

PF2.text: Mr. Rao confirmed with the affected resident that an active no-contact directive applies between the two students, and Oak Hall room 318 is the only currently available placement that keeps them separated; the re-entry plan must assign the student to Oak Hall room 318 and record a no-contact housing safeguard. He confirmed the vacancy after the draft packet was prepared, so the room assignment is not yet in the packet.

PF3.text: Dr. Bennett reviewed the student's counseling intake and documented a panic-disorder accommodation requiring conduct check-ins by secure video rather than in person, plus exactly two counseling appointments per week for the first four weeks after return. She finalized the recommendation after the draft packet was circulated, so it has not been added to the packet.

acceptance_conditions: The sanction must be a restorative agreement rather than a suspension.
Restitution must be set at exactly $250.
The student must be assigned to Oak Hall room 318.
A no-contact housing safeguard must be recorded as true.
Conduct check-ins must be conducted by secure video.
The student must have exactly two counseling appointments per week.
Counseling must continue for exactly four weeks after return.
A formal re-entry plan must be approved.

decisive_facts.why: The first-substantiated-violation finding changes the sanction from suspension to a restorative agreement and changes restitution from $500 to exactly $250.
The active no-contact directive and confirmed vacancy change the housing assignment to exactly Oak Hall room 318 and change the no-contact safeguard from absent to true.
The documented accommodation changes check-ins from in person to secure video and sets counseling at exactly two appointments per week for exactly four weeks.
